That's a great way to put it. And you need to conserve energy for that swing because it's not infinite. We treat our brains like laptops. plug them in, drink coffee, run at 100% forever, which is a biological lie.
Furuks found out the hard way. He's in a period of intense productivity, reading dense material 2 hours a day, furiously taking notes, doing everything right, according to hustle culture.
And then the wall, a brutal physical wall. A pulsing, heavy headache takes over his skull. His mind freezes. He literally cannot read a sentence or process simple thoughts for days.
He broke his brain through overuse. It's terrifying when the cognitive engine seizes up and it happens to high performers constantly.
The brain isn't a silicon hard drive. It's biological tissue. It consumes massive amounts of glucose and oxygen. You can't sprint indefinitely.
Mental energy is a finite fuel tank. If you don't schedule deliberate recovery, your biology will forcefully shut you down to protect itself.
You cannot out hustle biology. So, what does recovery look like for a pragmatist? Because the modern wellness industry has turned recovery into a competitive sport. Oh, absolutely.
